newsitem.title: EGYPT: Five people killed in two shootings in Egypt.
newsitem.headline: Five people killed in two shootings in Egypt.

text.p: A policeman shot and killed a suspected Moslem militant and another person while travelling on a train and three policemen were killed in another attack in southern Egypt on Saturday, security sources said.
"The officer identified Mohamed Abdel Moneim el-Farshouti and shot him dead with a passenger on the next seat," one said.
Another passenger was also wounded in the shooting near Sohag, 400 km (250 miles) south of Cairo, they added. The train was travelling from Luxor to Cairo.
The sources said Farshouti was a prominent leader of the Gama'a al-Islamiya (Islamic Group), the largest militant group fighting the Egyptian government, and was wanted for several attacks.

In a separate attack, gunmen thought to be Islamic militants shot dead three policemen and wounded six people at a police station in Deir Mawas, some 290 km (180 miles) south of Cairo, an interior ministry statement said.
Deir Mawas is near the town of Mallawi, which is the centre of activity of the Gama'a.
More than 1,000 people have been killed and hundreds wounded since the group launched its armed campaign in 1992.
